# Avinash (alvs.dev)

> Personal website of Avinash, a frontend engineer based in India with 4+ years of experience building web products. The site is part portfolio, part digital garden: it documents his work, projects, and current focus. He is the builder of Orbit, a daily budgeting app at orbitbudget.com, and is currently available for freelance, contract, or full-time work.

The site is a hand-built Astro project with a classless-stylesheet foundation and scoped custom styles. It intentionally avoids heavy frameworks, analytics bloat, and marketing language. Email is the best way to reach him; the listed address rotates periodically as spam prevention.

## Work With Me

* [Hire me](https://alvs.dev/hire-me): Most complete professional profile. Experience summary, core stack (Next.js, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS), featured projects, GitHub activity, and contact details. Currently available for freelance, contract, or full-time work.
* [Experience](https://alvs.dev/experience): Timeline of professional roles and freelance work.
* [Connect](https://alvs.dev/connect): Contact page with email, social profiles (LinkedIn, GitHub, Mastodon), response-time expectations, and the note that the email address changes periodically.

## Projects

* [Projects](https://alvs.dev/projects): Index of all projects with write-ups covering the problem, solution, engineering decisions, and tech stack.
* [Orbit](https://alvs.dev/projects/orbit): His main product: a daily budgeting app built around a single safe-to-spend number. Includes the offline-first architecture (IndexedDB queue + sync), Web Push via Supabase Edge Functions, custom Clerk auth flows, and the PWA approach. Live at [orbitbudget.com](https://www.orbitbudget.com).
* [alvs.dev](https://alvs.dev/projects/alvs): The story of this site itself: why Astro, the classless stylesheet philosophy, and the evolution from a hardcoded HTML page to the current build.
* [Lab](https://alvs.dev/lab): Small curiosity-driven HTML, CSS, and JS experiments.

## Writing

* [Notes](https://alvs.dev/notes): Public notes on web development and product thinking. Canonical source for his technical opinions, including his [skills and tools breakdown](https://alvs.dev/notes/skills-and-tools).
* [Changelog](https://alvs.dev/changelog): Ongoing record of changes to the site, useful for checking how current any page is.

## About

* [About](https://alvs.dev/about): Who he is, how he works, and personal interests.
* [Now](https://alvs.dev/now): What he is focused on right now: current projects, job search status, and what he's learning. The best page for up-to-date facts about him.
* [Uses](https://alvs.dev/uses): Gear, tools, and daily software.

## Optional

* [Sitemap](https://alvs.dev/sitemap): Full human-readable index of every page on the site.
* [Colophon](https://alvs.dev/colophon): How the site is built: stack, tooling, and open-source repo ([github.com/Av1-Lv5/alvs.dev](https://github.com/Av1-Lv5/alvs.dev)).
* [Radar](https://alvs.dev/radar): A running list of technologies he uses or is tracking, with no status or expertise claims.
* [Books](https://alvs.dev/books): What he has read.
* [Movies](https://alvs.dev/movies), [Podcasts](https://alvs.dev/podcasts): What he is listening to and watching.
* [Echoes](https://alvs.dev/echoes): Collected quotes and lines.
* [Feeds](https://alvs.dev/feeds): RSS feeds he follows and ways to follow his activity.
* [Guestbook](https://alvs.dev/guestbook): Visitors can leave a public message.
